q1_issues.issue: `QuantifierPhrase` takes a kind in its first slot, but the witness `sk_person_1` is put there; and the frequency adverb's other channel is unapplied — the event stays a single `Past` occurrence at strength 1.0 with no habitual rule and no strength set from "occasionally".
`(Inheritance ex_boyfriend boyfriend)` at 1.0/0.99 asserts that an ex-boyfriend is a boyfriend; "ex-" is privative, so the compound-kind genus is false here.
`(Possession michael_bergin baywatch)` encodes the bare noun-modifier "'Baywatch' hunk" with the genitive head, though the text has no 's, possessive pronoun, or of-phrase to license it.

The narrator's appositive identification (`(Member michael_bergin hunk)` and the Baywatch link) is sealed inside the reported speech, so it is asserted nowhere, although it is the reporter's own assertion rather than part of what she told John.

q2_gaps: privative / non-subsective modifiers ("ex-boyfriend", "former X") — the compound-kind genus rule licenses an `Inheritance` that the modifier explicitly cancels
discourse adverbial "in turn" — no licensed encoding, and the parse drops it

a frequency adverb over a past habitual with individuated participants ("occasionally told John") — the generic machinery needs a kind range and `QuantifierPhrase` needs a kind, neither of which a witness subject with a named recipient supplies

verb + preposition idiom ("sleep with") — the phrasal-verb fusion rule (keep `sleep_with` whole) and the prepositional-verb rule (object goes in the `With` oblique, never a direct-object role) both claim it, with no tiebreak
a proper-noun noun-modifier ("'Baywatch' hunk") — the compound rules bar fusing a name and offer no way to relate the named modifier to its head noun
notes: The antecedentless "she" as `sk_person_1`/`person`, the non-factive seal under `tell` with `Experiencer`+`Recipient`, and `Past`+`Ongoing`+`Still` for "was still sleeping" all follow the instruction set.
